name: Dusty midnight blue
lede: Dusty midnight blue is a near-black navy, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Konkikyō, "navy blue bellflower."

sections.title: A navy-blue bellflower
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[cobalt-blue]] and [[navy]], at Our library actually files this color under Purples rather than Blues, alongside the core color [[purple|Purple]], a reminder that a name and a database category do not always agree, and that this swatch reads as a near-black blue regardless [3].

Its nearest core app match is [[navy|Navy]], about 4.9 ΔE2000 units away [3]. The library's own ISCC-NBS mapping places it in the same block as several other 1920s names recorded by Maerz and Paul, including Homage Blue, dated to 1928 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the rarest colors : our archive finds it in only 37 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.16 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is Pietro Lorenzetti's *Madonna and Child Enthroned with Eight Angels*, dated to 1340, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Among sampled painters, Bronzino's twenty-one paintings contain it three times, a rate almost ninety-two times the archive's average, the sharpest spike, though built on a very small count [2]. It is also somewhat more common than average in paintings from the United Kingdom and Russia [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
